artboards.title: A · Pick up where you left off

annotations.text:
Three ways to make the home page more engaging, against what is there today.

Each one answers "why open this app right now" differently: A says because your next session is ready, B says because your streak is at stake, C says because there is a number to beat. They are not variations on a theme — pick the motivation first, and the layout follows.

Everything is drawn on the real tokens: #047857 accent, 16px radius, Bricolage Grotesque over JetBrains Mono, the existing card and button anatomy. Numbers are sample data.

As it is now.

The greeting and the momentum panel take the top third, then templates, then the button. Nothing on the screen is specific to today — the same page greets you whether you trained yesterday or three weeks ago, and the first concrete thing is a template name with a count.

A · Pick up where you left off

The session you would most likely repeat becomes the page: the actual exercises, the weights you last hit, one button. Momentum drops to a single row of day dots at the bottom.

Why: the common case is repeating a template, and this removes every step between opening the app and starting.

Tradeoff: it assumes you use templates. Without one it needs a real fallback, and it pushes stats almost out of sight.

B · Streak first

The streak becomes the whole top of the screen, with the best-ever mark as the thing to chase and an explicit "train today to keep it".

Why: a streak you can lose is the strongest reason to come back on a day you cannot be bothered.

Tradeoff: it cuts the other way when the streak breaks — the home page turns into a reminder of a bad month. It needs a deliberate, kind broken state, and that is real work. The dark block is also the only place in the app with a dark panel.

C · Beat last time

Leads with one concrete target: the lift you are due, what you did last time, and the next step up.

Why: progression is the reason people log at all, and a number to beat is sharper than a streak.

Tradeoff: it needs history to say anything, so it is empty for a new account and awkward when you turn up to train something else. The suggested weight also has to come from a rule you would need to define — the +2.5 shown here is a guess, not a computed target.

These mix.

A's next-session card with B's streak strip above it is a real fourth option, and probably the one I would build — the target line from C works as a single row inside A's card rather than as its own screen.

Say which motivation feels right and I will draw the combination properly rather than guessing at it.
